excerpts.text: Ticker: META. Stock Price: $598.86. FY2025 revenue of $200.97B, up 22% YoY. Family of Apps was 98.9% of revenue and Reality Labs was 1.1%. Market capitalization was about $1.52T.

Upcoming catalysts included the May 27, 2026 annual meeting, Q2 2026 revenue guidance of $58B-$61B, Q1 2026 revenue of $56.31B, higher ad impressions and average price per ad, a 2026 capex range raised to $125B-$145B, a $25B bond issuance to fund AI infrastructure, and the Muse model family.

The deck argues Meta trades at a discount because AI investments need to prove attractive returns. AI has improved advertising effectiveness, but monetization is not fully laid out. Management said weekly business-AI conversations grew 10x since the start of the year. AI investments reduce income available to shareholders.

Reality Labs has wide losses. The deck says smart glasses are doing well and daily users tripled year over year, but VR sustainability remains a management focus. Legal and regulatory issues warrant a valuation discount because voters and lawmakers have unfavorable views of social media.
The 80% confidence range showed bear/base/bull target prices of $616, $739, and $869, implying 3%, 23%, and 45% upside from the deck price.

Risks included advertising concentration, competition from TikTok, Alphabet, and Amazon, regulatory/litigation/antitrust exposure with high probability, and high-severity capital intensity and AI execution risk after capex guidance increased within one quarter.

The summary thesis emphasized 3.56B Family DAP, FY2025 revenue growth, network effects, cash generation, ROIC, operating discipline, smart glasses, Reality Labs pivot, AI improving ads, and a market price that the deck says reflects a bear scenario. It concluded: Meta is a good business, in a good industry, with good management, at a good price.
